title: Numbers: the step the database refuses
objective: Show with one boundary command that your model commits a transfer PostgreSQL refuses, forecast which segment of your claim's strip cracks, and record one remedy with the artifact it changes.

blocks.md: Your model's balance is a whole number with no bound. The database's is eight bytes. Stage 1 set that mismatch up as a seam, and this lesson is where it breaks.

choice.prompt: Recall S1.L5's table of what 64 bits mean. Which row does PostgreSQL's `bigint` take when a credit would pass the largest value it holds?

options.text: It never overflows; it keeps counting, like whole numbers.
options.why: `bigint` is eight bytes with a largest value. It does not grow.

options.text: It raises an out-of-range error and the statement fails.
options.why: The manual says attempts to store values outside the allowed range "will result in an error", and the recorded run raised SQLSTATE 22003 {{run:RUN-pg-claims}}.

options.text: It wraps, like Z3's signed BitVec 64.
options.why: BitVec 64 wraps {{run:RUN-z3-bv64}}. PostgreSQL takes a different row of the table.

options.text: It saturates at the maximum, then commits.
options.why: The manual's rule is an error, not a clamp.

blocks.md: Account 1 holds the largest `bigint` and account 2 holds 5. The credit is 1.
blocks.direction: The first SELECT is your model's step: the same credit in numbers with no bound. The UPDATE is the database's. Compare what each does.

call.prompt: Your model credits 1 to an account holding the largest `bigint`, and the database does the same credit. What outcome classes do they report?

options.why: The database cannot store the result.
The model has no bound, so nothing refuses on its side.

options.text: The model refused with `Insufficient`; PostgreSQL committed.
options.why: This reverses the direction of the failure. The model's guard passes.

options.text: The model committed; PostgreSQL raised an out-of-range error.
options.why: The model takes a step the database refuses.

blocks.after: The model's credit gave a balance one past the largest `bigint`. The database refused the same credit with SQLSTATE 22003 and left the balance as it was. The total over both accounts is a `numeric`, and it fits, although no single balance could hold it. {{run:RUN-pg-claims}}

blocks.md: Before the erosion fires, restate your claim from S2, CL-2.1, from memory. Its strip has three segments: the proposition of the model, the correspondence between model and system, and the requirement fit.

choice.prompt: Which segment of CL-2.1's strip cracks?

options.why: "Allowed implies succeeds" holds in the model and fails in the database. The two no longer match.
Conservation is still a theorem about whole numbers, and its proof is untouched.
The requirement, that money is neither made nor lost, is unchanged.

blocks.md:
The model's theorem still holds. What broke is the match between model and database, and the failure is a refusal, not a wrap. It is not retryable like a serialization failure either, because the same input fails again. Your claim from S6.L3, CL-6.1, gains a defeater too: its statistics showed the largest balance reached was far from the boundary.

Record one remedy as a decision, as you did in LAB-3.7. Each changes a different artifact.

1. **Bounded semantics.** The guard adds `bal(to) + amt <= 2^63 - 1`, and the S2 and S3 lemmas are re-proved. This changes the model.
2. **`Except Overflow`.** The database's out-of-range error maps to `Err Overflow`, and both sides report "refused: overflow". This changes the outcome type, and with it the relation R(S, D) that you define in S6.L8.
3. **`numeric` with a stated bound.** A `numeric(19,0)` column holds the balance `bigint` refuses and raises at its own declared bound {{run:RUN-pg-numeric-bound}}, so the bound must still appear in the semantics, or as an assumption. This changes the schema.

Drawer D-30, on Kani, is deferred. It appears in Today for the Rust `i64` path of your system, where `checked_add` returns `None` {{run:RUN-rust-i64}}. Nothing waits on it.

choice.prompt: Semantics V is `Except Overflow`: a credit past the largest `bigint` returns `Err Overflow` in the model, and your plan maps the database's out-of-range error to the same value. For the boundary command, credit 1 to an account holding the largest `bigint`, how do the model and the database compare?

options.text: They differ: the model takes a step the database refuses.
options.why: That was the unbounded model. Under V the model refuses too.

options.text: They differ: the database takes a step the model forbids.
options.why: The database refuses here, so it takes no step the model forbids.

options.text: They match: both sides refuse, and the outcomes are the same.
options.why: The model returns `Err Overflow`, and the database's error maps to it.

blocks.title: Production twin: TigerBeetle
blocks.md: TigerBeetle names overflow as a refusal result, `overflows_credits_posted` and its siblings (https://docs.tigerbeetle.com/reference/requests/create_transfers/, read 2026-10-23; pins in {{run:RUN-twin-pins}}). Which of your remedies does its interface match?

blocks.title: Build this
blocks.md: Add a boundary class to your generator and run the suite again. Record your remedy. Under the second remedy, the error map from LAB-6.3 gains `Overflow`.

notes: Recorded by W1-T12. values.cases.<case> holds, for each of the four cases, the statement, the error psql printed (null when the statement committed), the SQLSTATE the script echoed after a failed statement, the DETAIL line, and the balance after. Cite one as {{run:RUN-pg-numeric-bound#values.cases.<case>.sqlstate}}. Balances are strings: they exceed the integers JSON readers keep exact.

The server ran in postgres:18@sha256:74935e72241653ca55e0414067e6d8763aceb8a810eb51b452253ec3dcfc4336 (the digest RUN-scaffold pins) with --network none and --memory=6g and trust authentication, and was removed when the script finished. argv lists the three commands in order: the server's start, psql through docker exec and sh, and the removal; the exit code is psql's. Between the start and psql the recorder waited until docker logs w1t12-pg showed "PostgreSQL init process complete" and "database system is ready to accept connections" at least twice (the image's entrypoint first runs a temporary server for its initialization, which prints the first of them) and docker exec w1t12-pg pg_isready -U postgres exited 0, polling at most 120 times with a 0.5 s pause between polls; a psql started straight after the start finds no server socket and exits 2. psql's stdout and stderr were merged inside the container by 2>&1, so the log's lines are in the order psql wrote them (docker exec without a terminal carries the two streams apart, and its CLI prints them in no fixed order); the check psql-order fails a log in which an ERROR line comes after the sqlstate or balance echo that follows its statement.

Each case credits 1 at the edge of a type, S6.L4's boundary command: bigint at its largest value raises 22003 "bigint out of range" and keeps its balance [X RUN-pg-claims]; numeric(19,0) holds the same balance and the next one (its bound is 10^19, not bigint's); at 9999999999999999999 it raises 22003 "numeric field overflow" and keeps its balance; an unbounded numeric commits. The bound a column raises on is the one declared in its type.
LAST_ERROR_SQLSTATE keeps its value after a later success in psql, so the script echoes it only after a statement that failed.
Placeholder in argv: <sandbox>/pg is a scratch copy of numeric_bound.sql (the input lists it).

budget.harness_timeout_s is the wall time after which the recording script would have stopped each of the three commands in argv (600 s); started_at and duration_s are those of the psql command, the second.

The script ran on the PostgreSQL server of the Bench's service container image only. PGlite, the tab's engine, was not run on it: S1's six-row table is prose, and S6.L4 can add a PGlite configuration to this run if its cell shows remedy 3 in the tab.

RUN-rust-i64.title: Rust 1.96.0 i64: the dev profile panics on overflow, the release profile wraps, and checked_add returns None
verdict_lines: note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
b + x = -9223372036854775808 (wrapped; non-negativity broken; i128 total changed by -18446744073709551616)

stdout: b + x = -9223372036854775808 (wrapped; non-negativity broken; i128 total changed by -18446744073709551616)

notes: Recorded by W1-T12. values.debug and values.release hold what each binary did: debug.panicked and debug.panic_message (the dev profile's overflow check fired inside the source's catch_unwind), release.wrapped and release.b_plus_x (the release profile wrapped), and checked_add in both. Cite one as {{run:RUN-rust-i64#values.release.b_plus_x}}.

The crate is byte-identical to research/evidence/a2r3/rust (spine section 9.5: its source existed and its output was never committed); `record.mjs check` compares the copies. The program catches its own panic, so both binaries exit 0: the debug build's panic is the message on stderr and the line "b + x panicked (overflow check)" on stdout.

The two `Running` lines in the log show the exact rustc arguments: the dev profile (cargo's default) passes no -C opt-level, and the release profile passes -C opt-level=3. That the dev build checks overflow and the release build wraps is what the two binaries printed; the profile defaults that explain it are cargo's and rustc's documented ones [D]. The log keeps the panic's thread id verbatim (89 in this recording): it is the id of the main thread in the container's process numbering and not part of the result, and no check reads it. The two `Finished` lines carry cargo's own elapsed time, which differs between runs of the same command, so a replay can differ from this log on those lines.
stdout and stderr of each binary are printed in separate sections by rust_i64.sh, so the order of the two streams is never in question.
Placeholder in argv: <sandbox>/crate is a scratch copy of the crate (Cargo.toml and src/main.rs) with rust_i64.sh beside it (the inputs list them); the container sees it as /w.

budget.harness_timeout_s is the wall time after which the recording script would have stopped the docker run (600 s); started_at and duration_s are that docker run's, the container's start and both builds included.
